title: api-config-runtime-scratchpad
content:
API config / runtime sketch - scratchpad

Goal:
- Single inference API shape that covers hosted/dedicated/private with runtime-driven optimizations (batching, caching, quantization, routing).
- Keep client surface small: main request + optional config overrides (lightweight).
- Allow server-side policy to override unsafe knobs (e.g., quantization, fallback models).

Constraints / notes:
- Need to support streaming responses and function/tool calling.
- Backwards compatibility with current /v1/generate-ish endpoints is desirable but not required for first internal iteration.
- Typical users: platform teams, product engineers; some will embed config in route-level defaults (console).
- Security: ensure no user-supplied config can escalate privileges (routing to private tenants, etc).

Sketch: top-level request shape (proposal)

POST /v1/inference
Content-Type: application/json

Request body (client-facing simplified):
{
  "model": "open-redwood-7b-v2",               // optional: server can map aliases
  "input": "Translate to French: Hello world",
  "mode": "chat",                             // "generate" | "chat" | "embed"
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "stream": false,
  "config_overrides": {
    "batching": { "max_batch_tokens": 4096, "latency_target_ms": 200 },
    "kv_cache": { "enable": true, "ttl_seconds": 300 },
    "quantization": "q4_0",         // prefer server-side profile if disallowed
    "routing_policy": "cost_preferred"  // cost_preferred | latency_preferred | region:us-east-1
  },
  "metadata": { "request_id": "cli-123", "tags": ["mobile"] }
}

Server-side semantics (notes):
- config_overrides is advisory; server applies policy (org-level / route-level) -> server_final_config.
- If client requests incompatible quantization, server responds with 4xx or silently maps to closest allowed profile (TBD).
- routing_policy may pick dedicated vs hosted; fallback chain must be explicit in logs.

Example server_final_config (internal):
- model_variant: open-redwood-7b-v2-q4a
- cpu_worker: disabled
- gpu_pool: dedicated-sku-a
- batch_window_ms: 8
- max_batch_tokens: 4096
- kv_cache: enabled (prefix cache key = org+route+prompt-prefix hash)
- fallback_models: [open-redwood-3b, open-redwood-1.4b]
- streaming: true

YAML for route default (console-managed):
route: translate-fr
default_model: open-redwood-7b-v2
policies:
  allowed_quantizations: [q4_0, q8_0]
  routing: { priority: [dedicated, hosted], region: [us-east-1, eu-west-1] }
  max_latency_ms: 250
  cost_limit_per_1000_tokens_usd: 0.10

Runtime flow (ASCII):
Client --> API gateway (auth, rate limit) --> Router service (policy eval) --> Runtime pool (batcher + workers)
                                                      |-> KV cache (prefix)
                                                      |-> Model workers (GPU)
                                                      |-> Metrics/tracing

Key implementation questions / TODOs:
- How expressive should routing_policy be in client API vs console only? (expose cost vs latency hints)
- Cache key design: prefix-sensitive to allow prefix-KV caching without leaking sensitive PII. Need a hashing + salt approach.
- Batching windows: default 8ms but adaptive based on qps/latency SLO. Expose per-request hint (latency_target_ms).
- Fallback behavior: sync vs async? If primary overloaded, do we queue until timeout or immediately route to fallback?
- Streaming + batching: ensure chunked streaming works when request joined into batch (server fanout of tokens).

Open questions to discuss with SRE/Serving-runtime:
- Are there hard limits on per-request config size? console stores route YAML but client overrides should be small.
- Security review for routing hints (can't force private-only hardware).
- Observability: per-request token/latency/cost breakdown must include which fallback/quantization was used.

Mini prototyping notes (local hack plan):
- Implement a small HTTP handler that accepts the shape above and logs: policy decisions, final config, chosen worker id.
- Add a simple in-memory batcher with window 8ms/16ms and measure latency vs throughput on local stubs.
- Fake KV cache by prefix map and simulate hit-rate.

Example quick test payloads:
1) latency-sensitive mobile call:
{ "model": "open-redwood-7b-v2", "input": "Summarize: ...", "config_overrides": {"latency_target_ms": 100, "routing_policy": "latency_preferred"} }
2) high-throughput embeddings job on dedicated:
{ "mode": "embed", "model": "open-redwood-embed-2", "input": [... large array ...], "config_overrides": {"routing_policy": "dedicated_only", "batching": {"max_batch_tokens": 65536} } }

Notes to self (short):
- Keep client API small; majority of complexity should live in server policies/console.
- Add an admin-only field for "force_policy_override" for SRE only (for incident mitigation).
- Add tests for quantization mapping (requested -> allowed -> applied).

Related tickets/people:
- INF-482: routing policy MVP (Jamie owner)
- PR #927: runtime batching refactor (Aisha)

--end of scratchpad--
